 By Audrey Noble October 27, 2026 Photo: Spotlight/Launchmetrics Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story When people ask me what my favorite sunscreens are, I almost exclusively tell them about the French and Korean formulas that I hoard back from my travels (special shout-outs to the Caudalie Vinosun High Protection Glow Oil and Fromier EGF Cica Water Sun Ampoule ). The textures work better for my acne-prone skin and just feel so good when I slather them on. But the more impressive feat, of course, is the advanced formulations and ingredients that haven’t made their way to the US—until now. Earlier this year marked the first time since the 1990s that the US Food & Drug Administration has approved a new sunscreen filter to be used stateside: meet BEMT.
 Vogue’s Guide to BEMT Sunscreens
 Best Overall: La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 with BEMT , $40
 Best Blurred Finish: Ultra Violette Unblock Sunscreen SPF 50 , $40
 Best for Acne-Prone Skin: Neutrogena Face Sunscreen Acne-Prone Skin SPF 60 , $20
 Best for Dry Skin: Neutrogena Ultra Sheer Daily Face Sunscreen SPF 70 , $20
 More formally known as bemotrizinol , BEMT is a chemical sunscreen filter that protects against both UVA and UVB rays. Compared to other sunscreens in the States that combine different ingredients and filters to provide sun protection, BEMT works to protect skin not only from the UVB rays that cause skin cancer, but also the UVA rays that cause skin aging and hyperpigmentation in a single filter.
 Charlene Valledor, cosmetic chemist and president of SOS Beauty, adds that it is a more photostable ingredient and provides longer-lasting protection. Corinne Erickson, MD, board-certified dermatologist and owner of Georgia Skin Specialists, agrees and adds that it’s a large molecule that won’t absorb through the skin and into our bloodstreams, which is a main concern for many when it comes to chemical formulas. Sunscreens with BEMT also blend in more seamlessly and won’t leave behind a white cast, which makes it a great option for those with darker skin tones.
 But BEMT is not new and it’s been used by many parts of the world for decades. While this is an exciting development in the US sunscreen space, we’re still playing catch up ingredient-wise to places like Korea, Australia, and Europe. “It’s a step in the right direction, but we aren’t running to a better place yet,” says Charlotte Palermino, co-founder and chief brand officer of Dieux. “What I hope is that this opens the door to approving all the new and more innovative filters that would make America truly competitive globally.”
 “Brands and formulators have been trying to mimic the lightweight nature of the sunscreens from the EU and Korea using the approved filters in the US for years, but we’ve never been able to match them,” adds Valledor. “The new SPFs formulated with BEMT that are finally launching will be much closer to their international variants in texture.”
 And just because a sunscreen doesn’t have BEMT, it doesn’t mean they aren’t effective. Dr. Erickson says that it’s just great to have more options available to encourage more people to use sunscreen daily. “Because ultimately, if you love your sunscreen, you’re much more likely to wear it every day,” she says.
 So if this has piqued your interest and you’re curious how BEMT sunscreens actually perform, we’ve done the hard part and tested them for you. Read on to see which ones are actually worth it.

 Why We Love It: La Roche-Posay’s UVDefense packs quite a punch in the sun protection department. Along with the BEMT filter, you’ll also find that it comes with strong antioxidant protection so that your skin isn’t suffering against environmental stressors as well as broad-spectrum protection at SPF 50. But what makes it really stand out is its texture. It’s a light milky lotion that’s creamy smooth and absorbs so well into skin you almost forget that you’re wearing sunscreen, and it’s super hydrating (it boasts hydration for over 24 hours), making your skin feel extra soft and nourished. The feel of this sunscreen is just unmatched compared to the rest.
 Editor’s Experience: I trust any La Roche-Posay sunscreen and this one didn’t disappoint. My favorite part is its texture; it’s an incredibly lightweight, milky lotion that absorbs quickly into my skin and leaves it feeling really soft. It’s also super hydrating, which is always a nice added bonus, and it just feels so much better on my skin than a lot of the US sunscreens I’ve been wearing lately. I’ll definitely be adding this to my daily skincare routine and when people ask me for recs, I’ll be mentioning this.” — Audrey Noble, contributor

 Why We Love It: Made with oily and acne-prone skin in mind, this BEMT sunscreen controls excess oil production and blurs the appearance of pores without congesting them or causing more irritation. It’s super lightweight and feels airy when you put it on. But we especially love that it is a mineral formula, making it gentle and safe for even the most sensitive skin.
 Editor’s Experience: I love the lightweight feel, and its blurring effect really does reduce the appearance of my pores. But what impressed me most is how its matte finish, which I am usually never a fan of, doesn’t dry me out or make my complexion look dull. It does a great job controlling how shiny I can get, especially when I layer on makeup on top of my sunscreen. This will probably be my go-to when it gets super humid again. — A.N.

 Why We Love It: Another great option for those with acne-prone or oily skin, this BEMT sunscreen is a lightweight, non-comedogenic formula that does not clog pores and cause unwanted breakout. You’ll find BEMT and other known sun protection ingredients that will shield your skin from the sun’s harmful UV rays, but we especially love finding that it also has nourishing skin ingredients like niacinamide, vitamin E, and feverfew for antioxidant and hydrating benefits.
 Editor’s Experience: I was pleasantly surprised at how lightweight this sunscreen is. It absorbs really fast into the skin, making it a great layering product under makeup. Compared to many chemical sunscreens I’ve tried, this one feels great on my skin and its matte finish makes it so I don’t look too shiny and greasy. It’s a huge win for someone who gets very shiny often. — A.N.

It’s a great all-around option for every skin type.

 Everything You Need to Know 
 How do you use BEMT sunscreens?
 AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron The same basic sunscreen rules still apply. Dr. Erickson recommends looking for a sunscreen with broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher and be sure to use it everyday. You’ll want to use a shot glass full of sunscreen for your entire body, and reapply every two hours when outdoors and after swimming or sweating. “Even though BEMT is photostable, you still need to reapply your sunscreen,” she says.
 What are the downsides of BEMT?
 AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron BEMT sunscreens are generally safe. Valledor says that BEMT has been tested and ruled as generally safer and effective at concentrations up to 6%. Erickson also points to its already favorable safety profile, with it being a popular ingredient in sunscreens abroad. But as with any skin-care product, there’s always a slight risk of irritation. She recommends that those with allergy-prone or sensitive skin to read the full ingredient list to check if it contains ingredients that might cause a negative reaction. “It’s important to understand what is in the final formula in addition to BEMT to determine whether a formula is right for you and your skin type,” Valledor agrees.
 How We Tested
 AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. First, we lean on Vogue ’s vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—to gain professional insight on the industry’s standout products; ones specialists would actually use on and recommend to their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.
 As it relates to sunscreens, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: ingredients, texture, finish, SPF level, and the skin-care concerns they address. To do this, we paired our own personal tests of each formula with expert guidance and reviewer insights to determine which we would recommend to you.
